title: Optional finite PCAP dnscat2 cluster adapter
description: Coordinates one fixed assigned PCAP window through native Broker workers, HRW owners and a manager. Both sources finish and pass EOS, stream, semantic and ACK checks before shared state reduction. Source timestamps describe evidence time; findings are emitted during the later finite batch. Explicit finite_mode and assigned trace inputs are required; default startup disables live operation.

topics.title: Load the optional finite input Broker adapter
topics.description: @load selects the cluster framework, native Broker backend and adjacent main module. main remains independently loadable. This adapter coordinates one fixed, assigned finite PCAP window; the shared main module supplies DNS normalization and the session state machine.

topics.title: Apply process wide finite job lifetime and log settings
topics.description: exit_only_after_terminate keeps the process alive for EOF drain and acknowledgements. Rotation interval zero and an empty postprocessor command disable scheduled rotation/postprocessing; LogAscii::use_json selects JSON log output. These global redefs affect the whole dedicated finite job process.
links: Forward the standard Notice filter selectively

topics.title: Keep default raw log forwarding disabled
topics.description: Log::enable_remote_logging=F disables default remote log forwarding. DNCCluster scopes the adapter declarations. A later proxy specific initialization step enables only the existing Notice filter for remote forwarding.

topics.title: Require explicit finite mode
topics.description: finite_mode defaults to F and is redefinable. Startup emits LIVE_CLUSTER_DISABLED and terminates unless the process is configured for the finite assigned input contract. A finite worker also requires trace input.

ranges.code: const finite_mode = F &redef;

topics.title: Bound worker facts, owner facts and query tokens
topics.description: `max_worker_facts` bounds each worker buffer at 2048 observations by default. Owners retain at most 4096 facts and 4096 distinct query bindings. These metadata budgets bound one finite window’s storage and precommit scans. Overflow marks the window incomplete before authorized reduction.

topics.title: Name the fixed worker and owner sets
topics.description: expected_workers defaults to `worker-0` and `worker-1`; expected_owners defaults to `proxy-0` and `proxy-1`. These strings identify configured cluster roles and fixed view membership. The sequential source option also uses the `worker-0` and `worker-1` names explicitly.

ranges.code:
const expected_workers: set[string] = { "worker-0", "worker-1" } &redef;
const expected_owners: set[string] = { "proxy-0", "proxy-1" } &redef;

links: Release the configured second source after ACKs

topics.title: Select allowed observation namespaces
topics.description: allowed_scopes contains the permitted observation scope labels. The defaults are `site-1`, `scope-a`, `scope-b` and local. These configuration labels partition observed views; protocol envelopes, pairing and session progression provide the traffic evidence.

ranges.code: const allowed_scopes: set[string] = { "site-1", "scope-a", "scope-b", "local" } &redef;

links: Include scope in the typed owner key

topics.title: Bind a worker to its assigned packet inventory
topics.description: expected_packets and input_hash describe the worker’s assigned immutable input. sequential_sources controls transport release order after readiness. Its operational scheduling changes when a source is released, while source times and EOS determine reduction order and completeness.
links: Check native packet count and EOF

topics.title: Describe fixed source contents and time bounds
topics.description: Input holds packet count, supplied hash, a has_data flag and first/last source times. assigned_inputs maps worker names to those records. The configured runner binds actual file bytes and monotonic capture bounds; the adapter compares native observations with this declared inventory.
links: Compare the native close receipt with its assignment
Constrain source times to the assigned input

topics.title: Carry fixed membership and source assignments together
topics.description: View joins an id, node name to incarnation table and worker input table. The manager distributes this record once the configured native membership is ready. Receivers use its identities and inputs to validate the finite window.

topics.title: Define the typed stable correlation key
topics.description: Key contains schema version 1, observation scope, client/server addresses, typed server port, wrapper form, suffix and wire SID. HRW uses this typed record to route related observations. Worker identity and transaction identity stay in the fact envelope.
links: Derive the key from normalized metadata

topics.title: Bind a fact to worker, view and owner incarnations
topics.description: Fact carries the stable key, worker name and incarnation, fixed view id, selected owner topic and incarnation, and per owner sequence. These fields distinguish routing membership from the session key and let receipts reject a changed or mismatched destination.
links: Validate the source and target identities

topics.title: Preserve native source seconds alongside the observation
topics.description: `query_seconds` and `event_seconds` preserve native callback values as doubles. `token` identifies the namespaced transaction, and `o` carries compact Observation metadata. Owners reconstruct source time from those doubles before ordering and reduction, retaining the callback precision used by the shared lifecycle.
links: Restore native callback times on receipt
Supply source time to the shared lifecycle

topics.title: Name the closed per worker, per owner stream
topics.description: EOS identifies worker/incarnation, fixed view and destination owner. last_seq declares the final sequence number for that owner’s stream, including zero when the source sent that owner zero facts.
links: Send a close receipt to every owner

topics.title: Describe source completion and observation bounds
topics.description: EOS also retains packet count, supplied input hash, has_observation, first/last source times and complete. A genuinely empty input carries a false observation flag. Owners compare this receipt with the fixed assignment before preparing.

topics.title: Declare source, view and transport events
topics.description: The event interfaces carry post EOF handoff, Fact, EOS, installed View, node readiness and source release. They separate actual source closure, routing setup and observation transport.
links: Seal only after native EOF handling

topics.title: Declare receipt and preparation acknowledgements
topics.description: fact_ack and eos_ack return owner receipts to workers. ack_seen conveys those receipts to the manager, while prepared supplies each owner’s complete flag and fact count. Publication acceptance and these observed acknowledgements are separate stages.
links: Wait for votes and ACK inventory

topics.title: Declare commit, completion and failure controls
topics.description: commit_window authorizes shared lifecycle reduction for a view. owner_done reports an owner’s reduction completion; failure and finish coordinate an incomplete or completed finite job shutdown.
links: Enter reduction once per authorized owner

topics.title: Expose redefineable publication and ordering hooks
topics.description: publish_fact returns transport publication acceptance, and publication_order returns the outgoing Fact vector. Both are marked &redef. Native defaults use HRW publication and preserve the vector’s order.

ranges.code:
global publish_fact: function(f: Fact): bool &redef;
global publication_order: function(f: Facts): Facts &redef;

topics.title: Label local diagnostic receipts
topics.description: Trace begins with action, native node name, worker, owner, token, view id and sequence. Defaults supply the local node and empty optional identities. These labels make control and transport stages distinguishable in local stdout receipts.

topics.title: Represent counts and observed source times
topics.description: Trace packets/facts count observed work, complete reports the current outcome, and has_observation distinguishes an empty source. observed and source_query carry source event and original query times; uid retains observed connection identity.

topics.title: Keep diagnostic source time distinct from local time
topics.description: The remaining Trace fields describe scope, SID, kind, route, generation and detail. exact_time can retain a full precision source value. local_network defaults to network_time for diagnostics, while lifecycle expiry and ordering use the explicit source clock.

topics.title: Print operational receipts as JSON
topics.description: trace converts the supplied Trace record to JSON and prints it to standard output. These local operational receipts explain transport and completeness; the shared main module emits security findings through the standard Notice framework.

ranges.code: function trace(t: Trace) { print to_json(t); }

links: Locate the shared security emission path
Read aggregate cache counts at exit

topics.title: Latch the finite view and failure publication
topics.description: view and installed retain the accepted fixed configuration. bad marks an incomplete window; failure_sent bounds operational failure publication. finished, view_sent, current_nodes and view_ready track the one view setup and finish lifecycle.

topics.title: Retain worker packet and closure progress
topics.description: packets, source_first and source_last record actual packet callbacks. source_eof and sealed distinguish native close from post EOF handoff. source_dropped counts late or overflowing facts; started and sent gate the one finite publication pass.

topics.title: Retain bounded source facts and stream receipts
topics.description: source_buffer holds selected worker Observations. seq_count indexes per owner outgoing sequences. ack_counts is declared here; active manager ACK bookkeeping uses the separate receipt sets. eos_seen, received and transport_hash retain source closes, unique sequence counts and content digests. facts holds the owner’s finite reduction input.

topics.title: Retain owner token bindings and source clock
topics.description: owner_prepared and owner_committed gate reduction. token_bindings maps stable key plus namespaced token to an owner admitted Frame; fact_identity deduplicates query and paired semantics separately. source_clock advances during sorted reduction.

topics.title: Track prepare votes, ACK sets and shutdown
topics.description: prepare_votes/counts retain owner readiness. Global fact and EOS ACK sets deduplicate manager receipts, done_owners tracks reduction completion, and decision_sent/shutdown_scheduled gate the finite commit and shutdown paths.
links: Finish after all owners report completion

topics.title: Choose query or actual reply source time
topics.description: event_time returns reply_at for a paired observation and at for a query observation. The original query time stays in Observation even when its paired event sorts later.

ranges.code:
function event_time(o: DNScat2::Observation): time
{ if ( o?$reply ) return o$reply_at; return o$at; }

topics.title: Bind semantic content and full precision native times
topics.description: observation_digest hashes the JSON metadata together with query/reply seconds formatted at 17 significant digits. This includes native time precision beyond JSON display rounding, so changed fine grained time content can be distinguished from a duplicate.

topics.title: Build a typed owner key from normalized fields
topics.description: `key_for` combines scope, client and server addresses, typed server port, wrapper form, suffix and SID. These observed protocol fields define the HRW key. Related traffic keeps one effective owner across UDP source port changes and worker observations, preserving its lifecycle context.

topics.title: Collect only finite worker observations
topics.description: remote_dispatch starts with an empty Frame and accepts observations only on a WORKER with finite_mode enabled. The adapter replaces the core dispatch callback with this function, leaving the common lifecycle for later owner reduction.
links: Buffer metadata with cleared worker bindings

topics.title: Latch late facts or worker buffer overflow
topics.description: A sealed source or full max_worker_facts buffer increments source_dropped and marks bad. The first such failure emits a local SOURCE_INCOMPLETE receipt; failure_sent permits at most one installed view manager failure publication on this path. The observation returns an empty Frame.
links: Read the shared operational failure latch

topics.title: Buffer compact metadata with cleared worker bindings
topics.description: The worker clears generation, original key binding, context and progressed priority, then buffers compact Observation metadata. Frame lengths, kinds, SID, suffix and key fingerprints carry the lifecycle inputs. Raw query and answer bytes remain in local carrier normalization. Returning the request Frame preserves native DNS pairing until the owner assigns an epoch.
links: Assign the original query’s owner binding

topics.title: Override the shared lifecycle with sorted source time
topics.description: `owner_clock` returns sorted `source_clock` on a PROXY and native `network_time` elsewhere. Separate redefs select observation dispatch and lifecycle time. Each reduced fact advances the source clock before shared expiry and promotion, preserving the source timing of state transitions.
links: Advance the clock before each reduction
Use the preserved completing source timestamp

topics.title: Use native proxy pool HRW publication
topics.description: native_publish sends a Fact through Cluster::publish_hrw using proxy_pool and the typed key. native_order preserves the outgoing vector. The redefs install these defaults behind the explicit publication hooks.

topics.title: Mark incompleteness and bound failure publication
topics.description: mark_bad sets bad and prints INCOMPLETE with its reason. An installed nonmanager node sends one manager failure event, guarded by failure_sent. Repeated failures keep the incomplete state while the operational publication latch bounds control traffic.
links: Drain and stop the finite window

topics.title: Require a sealed source and unchanged owner view
topics.description: worker_maybe_send requires finite WORKER role, installed view, source release, sealed EOF and an unsent source. It checks the live proxy count and each configured owner incarnation against the frozen view before setting sent and constructing outgoing facts.

topics.title: Route each typed key to one configured owner
topics.description: Each buffered Observation supplies a typed key to `Cluster::hrw_topic`. The selected topic must name a configured owner. Related keys select one effective owner, preserving session context across workers and UDP source ports. Each owner stream increments its own contiguous sequence count.

topics.title: Construct the namespaced transaction envelope
topics.description: The Fact binds worker incarnation, view id, selected owner incarnation and sequence. It retains native query/event seconds and formats token as worker/incarnation/UID/DNS ID/serial. A reused UID or DNS ID remains distinct across workers, incarnations and fresh transaction serials.

topics.title: Publish the ordered outgoing vector
topics.description: publication_order supplies the outgoing vector. Each Fact then passes to publish_fact. FACT_SEND records publication acceptance; a false return marks bad. Actual owner receipt and worker ACKs are tracked separately before manager commit.

topics.title: Send EOS to every configured owner
topics.description: Each worker sends an EOS for every owner, including a zero fact stream. last_seq uses that owner’s count, while native packet inventory and first/last times describe the entire assigned worker input. complete requires native EOF, an unmarked source and the expected packet count.
links: Compare EOS with the fixed source assignment
Represent an empty source through actual packet bounds

topics.title: Wait for owner votes and measured receipt inventory
topics.description: The manager requires its role, an unsent decision, one prepare vote per owner and an EOS ACK for every worker owner combination. It totals owner fact counts, combines their complete flags with bad, and waits until the global fact ACK set covers that total.

topics.title: Commit only the complete closed window
topics.description: `decision_sent` latches one decision. An incomplete window traces `WINDOW_INCOMPLETE` and schedules shutdown. A complete window traces `WINDOW_COMMIT` and sends `commit_window` to proxies. Both assigned inputs have closed and passed EOS, stream, semantic and ACK checks before reduction emits findings; their timestamps retain source evidence time.
links: Preserve evidence time at the actual emitter

topics.title: Sort finite facts by actual source event time
topics.description: `compare_facts` orders the complete finite set by actual source event time: query `at` or paired `reply_at`. Sorting follows the complete window decision. The shared lifecycle therefore sees the source sequence after all assigned input and receipt checks finish.

topics.title: Order tied queries before pairs and INIT before other queries
topics.description: At equal event time, query facts precede paired facts and INIT queries precede other queries. strcmp on the namespaced token breaks remaining ties. Different INIT keys at the same stable key/time are rejected during preparation before this ordering can choose a winner.
links: Prevalidate ambiguous equal time key changes

topics.title: Require every sequence declared by both EOS sources
topics.description: Preparation begins once per owner after EOS arrives from all expected workers. Each EOS must be complete and its final sequence count must equal unique received facts. The loop also checks every transport_hash entry from 1 through last_seq within the fact bound, exposing gaps even when EOS itself arrived.
links: Accept the matching source close identity
Withhold reduction for an incomplete window

topics.title: Reject conflicting equal time INIT barriers before reduction
topics.description: The barriers table indexes stable key and query source time. Two request only kind 3 observations at that index must carry the same client key fingerprint. A difference marks bad before any owner prepare vote can authorize shared state reduction.
links: Apply deterministic ordering to the remaining valid ties

topics.title: Prevalidate repeated token content
topics.description: semantics indexes stable key, namespaced token and query versus pair role. Repeated entries must share observation_digest. Query observations are also retained by key/token for pair consistency checks. These checks scan the whole closed fact set before commit.
links: Include full precision times in the content identity
Require the pair’s original query metadata

topics.title: Check token and semantic budgets before commit
topics.description: The complete set may contain at most max_tokens distinct key/token queries and max_owner_facts semantic entries. Exceeding either sets bad before the prepare vote, keeping capacity rejection ahead of Notice producing reduction.

ranges.code: if ( |queries|>max_tokens || |semantics|>max_owner_facts ) bad=T;

topics.title: Require an original query with identical transaction metadata
topics.description: Each paired fact must have a query at the same stable key and namespaced token. Its request Frame, native query time, UID, DNS ID, serial, query type/hash and typed peers must match that query. A missing query or changed metadata marks the window incomplete before reduction.
links: Retain the original query’s admitted owner Frame

topics.title: Send the owner’s complete window preparation result
topics.description: PREPARED reports the current complete flag and retained fact count. The owner publishes that same flag/count with its native incarnation and fixed view id to the manager. This is a readiness vote; the manager sends the separate commit authorization.

ranges.code:
trace([$action="PREPARED",$owner=Cluster::node,$complete=!bad,$facts=|facts|]);
Cluster::publish(Cluster::manager_topic,prepared,Cluster::node,Cluster::node_id(),view$id,!bad,|facts|);

links: Combine both owner votes and ACKs

topics.title: Validate the fixed source and destination identities
topics.description: validate_fact requires an installed view, matching view id, configured worker incarnation, this owner’s node topic and current owner incarnation. The following checks then examine the compact Observation and request Frame.

topics.title: Bound scope and compact request metadata
topics.description: Scope must belong to allowed_scopes and fit 128 bytes. UID, local token, envelope token, suffix and key fingerprint have explicit bounds. The request must arrive with empty context/original key binding and generation zero, leaving owner lifecycle admission responsible for those fields.

ranges.code: if ( o$scope !in allowed_scopes || |o$scope|>128 || |o$uid|>128 || |o$token|>256 || |f$token|>512 || |q$suffix|==0 || |q$suffix|>253 || |q$key_hash|>64 || |q$context|>0 || q$generation!=0 || |q$initial_key_hash|>0 ) return F;

links: Clear worker lifecycle bindings before buffering

topics.title: Validate frame shape, canonical token and typed key
topics.description: The request must be valid, with a four lowercase hex SID, supported kind, bounded length, DNS ID at most 65535, positive serial and bounded positive sequence. The token must exactly reproduce worker/incarnation/UID/DNS ID/serial; question_hash must be 64 lowercase hex characters, and the supplied key must equal key_for(o).

topics.title: Constrain native times to assigned PCAP bounds
topics.description: The worker input must contain data. Query seconds must lie within its first/last interval expanded by one microsecond for classic PCAP representation, and event seconds must be at or after query seconds and within the upper bound. A query only event requires equal query/event seconds. This tolerance bounds numeric representation; EOS and sequence coverage establish completeness.
links: Require complete EOS and sequence coverage

topics.title: Check the compact paired reply fields
topics.description: A paired observation requires reply_at and a valid reply Frame, with bounded key fingerprint, supported kind and bounded length. Passing these final metadata checks returns T to the owner receipt handler.

ranges.code:
if ( o?$reply && (! o?$reply_at || ! o$reply$valid || |o$reply$key_hash|>64 || o$reply$kind>3 || o$reply$length>DNScat2::max_frame_bytes) ) return F;
return T;

links: Match the pair to its original query

topics.title: Count actual native packet callbacks
topics.description: raw_packet acts only for a finite WORKER. It increments packets, records source_first on the first packet and updates source_last from network_time. These actual observations support the assigned input close check.
links: Compare the source’s final native inventory

topics.title: Accept native EOF for the assigned finite trace
topics.description: Pcap::file_done requires finite WORKER role and one source close. It rejects remote events, a different assigned input path, a nontrace source or an already finished process. It records EOF, compares packet count and hash length, traces the native close and queues after_eof for callback drain.
links: Seal during the queued post EOF handoff

topics.title: Seal the buffered source after the native close callback
topics.description: The queued after_eof event sets sealed=T and tries worker_maybe_send. Publication additionally requires readiness and release, so native EOF and the transport handshake can complete in either operational order.

ranges.code: event after_eof() { sealed=T; worker_maybe_send(); }

topics.title: Reject changed or unconfigured membership
topics.description: `node_up` requires finite mode and configured worker, owner or manager membership. It rejects a changed incarnation from the installed view. On the manager, the active worker and proxy counts and complete input assignment table gate construction of the initial fixed view.

topics.title: Freeze node incarnations and assigned inputs
topics.description: The manager marks view_sent, copies each expected worker and owner incarnation, and creates a finite view id from its native node_id. assigned_inputs accompanies the same view. This freezes one membership/input assignment for the window.

topics.title: Publish the frozen view to workers and proxies
topics.description: The manager sends install_view to worker_topic and proxy_topic, then traces VIEW_SENT. Readiness ACKs from these recipients gate source release.

topics.title: Invalidate a fixed view node disconnect
topics.description: During an installed unfinished finite window, node_down marks bad when the departed node belongs to the frozen view. The failure path drains and stops the job; state ownership remains bound to that one view.

topics.title: Validate fixed view cardinality and source bindings
topics.description: A recipient installs one finite view. Node/input counts must match configuration, its own native incarnation must match the view, and each expected worker needs a node identity and an input with a 64 character hash. It then copies the View and marks installed.

topics.title: Acknowledge the accepted view with native identity
topics.description: VIEW_INSTALLED records the view id, then ready_ack sends this node’s name, native incarnation and accepted view id to the manager. The manager validates those identities before counting readiness.

ranges.code:
trace([$action="VIEW_INSTALLED",$view_id=view$id]);
Cluster::publish(Cluster::manager_topic,ready_ack,Cluster::node,Cluster::node_id(),view$id);

links: Require the configured complete readiness set

topics.title: Require every fixed view node’s readiness
topics.description: The manager accepts ready_ack only for the installed view and matching configured incarnation. view_ready is a set, so repeated ACKs retain one readiness entry. The full worker plus owner cardinality opens the source release branch.
links: Choose concurrent or sequential publication release

topics.title: Choose operational source release order
topics.description: With sequential_sources, the manager initially releases `worker-0`. Otherwise it sends start_source to every expected worker. This schedules transport publication of already bounded sources; native source timestamps determine later reduction order.

ranges.code:
if ( sequential_sources ) Cluster::publish(Cluster::node_topic("worker-0"),start_source,"worker-0",view$id);
else for ( w in expected_workers ) Cluster::publish(Cluster::node_topic(w),start_source,w,view$id);

topics.title: Accept release only for this installed worker/view
topics.description: start_source requires WORKER role, this worker name, an installed view and matching view id. It sets started and tries publication. A source already sealed at EOF can now send; an open source still waits for its native close.
links: Require both sealed input and release

topics.title: Reject invalid or post preparation facts
topics.description: Only PROXY handles Fact. An owner already prepared or a failed validate_fact marks the window incomplete and returns. This prevents a prepared closed set from absorbing later data.

topics.title: Restore exact source callback times before content hashing
topics.description: The owner reconstructs o.at from query_seconds and a paired reply_at from event_seconds. The transport digest combines the full Fact JSON with observation_digest, retaining exact native time content in duplicate checks.
links: Order by the reconstructed source event time

topics.title: Recognize identical sequence delivery and reject conflicts
topics.description: A repeated worker/sequence must carry the same transport digest. Changed content calls mark_bad. The owner traces FACT_DUPLICATE and ACKs the sequence with the current accepted flag, then returns before adding another fact.
links: Also check key/token content before commit

topics.title: Bound unique owner fact retention
topics.description: At max_owner_facts the owner marks incomplete and refuses storage. Otherwise it stores the worker/sequence digest, increments that worker’s unique received count and appends the Fact. A duplicate sequence followed the earlier return path.

ranges.code:
if ( |facts|>=max_owner_facts ) { mark_bad("bounded owner fact buffer overflow"); return; }
transport_hash[f$worker,f$seq]=digest; ++received[f$worker]; facts[|facts|]=f;

links: Compare unique receipt coverage with EOS

topics.title: Trace the admitted fact and acknowledge receipt
topics.description: FACT_RX records source and query times, namespaced token, routing key digest and stage kinds. fact_ack then confirms that stored sequence to its worker. This receipt is later relayed to the manager as observed transport progress.

ranges.code:
trace([$action="FACT_RX",$worker=f$worker,$owner=Cluster::node,$seq=f$seq,$token=f$token,$observed=event_time(f$o),$source_query=f$o$at,$uid=f$o$uid,$scope=f$o$scope,$sid=f$key$sid,$route=sha256_hash(to_json(f$key)),$kind=f$o?$reply ? "PAIR" : "QUERY",$frame_kind=f$o$request$kind,$reply_kind=f$o?$reply ? f$o$reply$kind : 255]);
Cluster::publish(Cluster::node_topic(f$worker),fact_ack,Cluster::node,f$seq,T);

topics.title: Validate EOS identity and repeated close content
topics.description: EOS requires installed PROXY role, the configured worker incarnation, accepted view id, this owner name and a bounded last_seq. A repeated worker EOS must be JSON identical; changed close content marks incomplete and returns.

topics.title: Compare native source close with its assigned input
topics.description: The EOS complete flag, input hash, packet count, observation flag and first/last source times must match the view’s worker assignment. A difference sets bad. The owner retains the EOS for stream completeness checks even when the window is incomplete.

topics.title: Acknowledge EOS and try owner preparation
topics.description: EOS_RX reports the observed close and current completeness. The owner sends eos_ack to the worker, then owner_maybe_prepare checks whether both fixed sources have closed with full sequence coverage and consistent semantics.
links: Inspect the closed stream preparation gate

topics.title: Relay actual fact receipt to the manager
topics.description: fact_ack traces owner, sequence and accepted status, then publishes ack_seen with this worker’s native incarnation and is_eos=F. Manager ACK bookkeeping tracks the owner/worker sequence namespace separately from publish acceptance.

topics.title: Relay actual EOS receipt to the manager
topics.description: eos_ack records the owner’s last_seq and local source_eof status, then publishes ack_seen with is_eos=T. The manager tracks one close ACK per worker owner pair.
links: Collect the complete EOS ACK matrix

topics.title: Validate and deduplicate manager ACK inventory
topics.description: ack_seen requires MANAGER role, installed view, configured worker incarnation and configured owner. An excessive sequence marks bad. EOS adds a worker/owner set member; a fact ACK adds worker/owner/sequence, so repeats retain one inventory entry.
links: Compare the ACK set with prepared counts

topics.title: Release `worker-1` after both `worker-0` close ACKs
topics.description: The optional sequential branch requires `worker-0` and an unreleased second source. It checks every expected owner’s `worker-0` EOS ACK before latching worker1_released and sending `worker-1` its start event. This is transport scheduling, while the whole window commit still waits for all sources.

topics.title: Reconsider the manager decision after ACK updates
topics.description: After ACK bookkeeping and optional source release, manager_maybe_decide reevaluates the complete vote/receipt gate. The same gate is also reconsidered when prepare votes arrive.

ranges.code: manager_maybe_decide();

links: Require complete votes and ACK coverage

topics.title: Accept an owner vote for this exact view/incarnation
topics.description: prepared requires MANAGER role, installed view, configured owner and matching owner incarnation. It records that owner’s complete flag and fact count, then rechecks the manager decision gate.
links: Join the votes with ACK receipts

topics.title: Enter source sorted reduction once after complete commit
topics.description: commit_window requires installed PROXY role, matching view, a clean prepared owner and an uncommitted window. It latches owner_committed and sorts facts with compare_facts. Both assigned inputs have finished before this finite batch reduction begins.

topics.title: Advance source time for each sorted fact
topics.description: For each sorted Fact, source_clock becomes its actual event_time. is_reply identifies query versus paired metadata, and observation_digest supplies semantic content for reduction deduplication. The shared lifecycle_time override reads this source_clock.
links: Supply the clock to shared state expiry

topics.title: Deduplicate key/token semantics during reduction
topics.description: fact_identity indexes stable key, namespaced token and query/pair role. An identical repeated semantic fact advances to the next entry. Conflicting content or a full reduction cache marks incomplete and breaks the loop. The earlier whole window preparation is responsible for rejecting such conflicts and capacity excess before commit.

topics.title: Save the owner admitted Frame under its original query token
topics.description: The owner calls `DNScat2::local_dispatch` for the sorted query and stores its admitted Frame under stable key plus namespaced token. The Frame retains the owner assigned generation and original key binding. A paired fact retrieves this original admission, so stale replies reach the shared generation guard with the correct epoch.
links: Reuse that original binding for the paired reply

topics.title: Invoke the shared main emitter with the original query binding
topics.description: A pair requires a valid original `token_bindings` entry. The owner restores that Frame and calls `DNScat2::local_dispatch`; missing or refused admission traces `UNKNOWN_QUERY` and skips. The shared main emitter applies generation and stage guards. Finite batch emission follows input closure and commit, with `ts` preserving completing source evidence time.
links: Trace the original owner epoch binding
Use source time for lifecycle decisions
Forward the shared standard Notice output

topics.title: Report completion of the finite reduction pass
topics.description: OWNER_DONE traces the fact count, complete flag and final source clock, with an explicit observation flag. owner_done then reports owner identity/incarnation, view id and fact count to the manager.

ranges.code:
trace([$action="OWNER_DONE",$owner=Cluster::node,$facts=|facts|,$complete=!bad,$observed=source_clock,$has_observation=|facts|>0]);

topics.title: Finish after every owner reports reduction completion
topics.description: The manager validates owner/view/incarnation before adding done_owners. Once its cardinality equals expected_owners and shutdown is unscheduled, it schedules finish in one second. That interval is an operational drain delay.

topics.title: Drain and stop an operationally incomplete window
topics.description: For the installed view, the manager sets `bad` and traces `WINDOW_FAILURE`. It schedules shutdown after one second so diagnostics and ACK traffic can drain. The complete source decision gate controls commit authorization.
links: Separate incomplete shutdown from commit authorization

topics.title: Remotely enable only the standard Notice filter on proxies
topics.description: The priority `-10` initialization handler runs this filter change for finite PROXY role. It retrieves Notice::LOG’s default filter, sets log_remote=T and replaces the filter. Default remote DNS/connection log forwarding stays disabled by the global policy; the shared main Notice is the security output forwarded here.
links: Read the default remote forwarding policy
Locate the shared emitter call path

topics.title: Require explicit finite trace operation at startup
topics.description: At priority `-20`, `finite_mode=F` prints `LIVE_CLUSTER_DISABLED` and terminates the process. A finite WORKER requires `reading_traces()`. Accepted configuration prints INIT with engine version, backend and node role. The job buffers its assigned PCAP window until native EOF, receipt validation and manager commit authorize reduction.
links: Read the disabled by default setting

topics.title: Publish finite window shutdown and terminate
topics.description: finish sets finished=T. On the manager it publishes finish to worker and proxy topics, then every recipient traces FINISH with its current completeness and calls terminate. exit_only_after_terminate makes this explicit completion path part of the finite job.
links: Retain processes until the explicit finish path

topics.title: Print aggregate finite buffer and ACK state at exit
topics.description: zeek_done prints CLUSTER_STATS with node name, retained source/owner facts, source drops, transport and semantic entries, query bindings, fact ACKs, EOS sources and configured caps. The counts describe one process/view at exit. Shared main health counters separately describe candidate/session outcomes and FIFO invariants.

topics.title: Retain explicit empty source time state
topics.description: A source begins with zero packets and zero first/last times. raw_packet supplies real bounds only when a packet exists; EOS uses packets>0 as has_observation. Empty assigned input therefore closes with a false observation flag and its declared empty bounds.

ranges.code:
global source_first = double_to_time(0);
global source_last = double_to_time(0);

links: Set times only from actual packet callbacks

topics.title: Follow closed input authorization to the shared emitter
topics.description: EOS sequence coverage and semantic preparation precede the manager’s commit. Owners then source sort the closed set and invoke the shared main lifecycle. Notice timestamps preserve source evidence time, while finite window emission occurs after all input completion and commit.

topics.title: Follow the original owner query binding into a late pair
topics.description: The worker transports unbound metadata. During sorted reduction, the query obtains an owner admitted Frame and token_bindings retains it. The pair retrieves that original Frame before shared lifecycle processing, preserving the generation fence across replacement and expiry.
